This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# ascii-image-converter

ascii-image-converter is a command-line tool that converts images into ASCII art and prints them to the console. It supports common image formats and provides options for colored output, braille art, saving output to files, and more.

Supported input formats:
- JPEG/JPG
- PNG
- BMP
- WEBP
- TIFF/TIF
- GIF

Basic CLI usage:

    ascii-image-converter [image paths/urls]

Example:

    ascii-image-converter myImage.jpeg

Common flags (summary):
- -C, --color        : Display ASCII art with colors from the original image
- -b, --braille       : Use braille characters instead of ASCII
- --threshold         : Threshold value for braille conversion (0-255)
- --dither            : Apply dithering for braille output
- -d, --dimensions    : Set width,height in characters (e.g. -d 60,30)
- -W, --width         : Set output width in characters
- -H, --height        : Set output height in characters
- -m, --map           : Provide a custom character map (darkest -> lightest)
- -g, --grayscale     : Output in grayscale
- -n, --negative      : Output in negative colors
- -c, --complex       : Use a more complex character set for detail
- -f, --full          : Fit output to terminal width while maintaining aspect ratio
- -s, --save-img      : Save ASCII art as a PNG image
- --save-txt          : Save ASCII art as a TXT file
- --save-gif          : Save GIFs as ASCII art GIFs (experimental)
- --font              : Path to .ttf font when saving images/gifs
- --font-color        : RGB value for font color when saving
- --save-bg           : RGBA background color when saving
- --formats           : Display supported input formats

Notes:
- Braille and color output depend on terminal/font support.
- GIF conversion/support may be limited for some GIFs.

For license information, see LICENSE or LICENSE.txt in the repository.
---
all.gif
braille.gif
color.gif
dimensions.gif
dither.gif
map.gif
negative.gif
save.gif
</output>

This tool converts images into ascii art and prints them on the terminal.
Further configuration can be managed with flags.

Usage:
  ascii-image-converter [image paths/urls or piped stdin] [flags]

Flags:
  -C, --color             Display ascii art with original colors
                          If 24-bit colors aren't supported, uses 8-bit
                          (Inverts with --negative flag)
                          (Overrides --grayscale and --font-color flags)
                          
      --color-bg          If some color flag is passed, use that color
                          on character background instead of foreground
                          (Inverts with --negative flag)
                          (Only applicable for terminal display)
                          
  -d, --dimensions ints   Set width and height for ascii art in CHARACTER length
                          e.g. -d 60,30 (defaults to terminal height)
                          (Overrides --width and --height flags)
                          
  -W, --width int         Set width for ascii art in CHARACTER length
                          Height is kept to aspect ratio
                          e.g. -W 60
                          
  -H, --height int        Set height for ascii art in CHARACTER length
                          Width is kept to aspect ratio
                          e.g. -H 60
                          
  -m, --map string        Give custom ascii characters to map against
                          Ordered from darkest to lightest
                          e.g. -m " .-+#@" (Quotation marks excluded from map)
                          (Overrides --complex flag)
                          
  -b, --braille           Use braille characters instead of ascii
                          Terminal must support braille patterns properly
                          (Overrides --complex and --map flags)
                          
      --threshold int     Threshold for braille art
                          Value between 0-255 is accepted
                          e.g. --threshold 170
                          (Defaults to 128)
                          
      --dither            Apply dithering on image for braille
                          art conversion
                          (Only applicable with --braille flag)
                          (Negates --threshold flag)
                          
  -g, --grayscale         Display grayscale ascii art
                          (Inverts with --negative flag)
                          (Overrides --font-color flag)
                          
  -c, --complex           Display ascii characters in a larger range
                          May result in higher quality
                          
  -f, --full              Use largest dimensions for ascii art
                          that fill the terminal width
                          (Overrides --dimensions, --width and --height flags)
                          
  -n, --negative          Display ascii art in negative colors
                          
  -x, --flipX             Flip ascii art horizontally
                          
  -y, --flipY             Flip ascii art vertically
                          
  -s, --save-img string   Save ascii art as a .png file
                          Format: <image-name>-ascii-art.png
                          Image will be saved in passed path
                          (pass . for current directory)
                          
      --save-txt string   Save ascii art as a .txt file
                          Format: <image-name>-ascii-art.txt
                          File will be saved in passed path
                          (pass . for current directory)
                          
      --save-gif string   If input is a gif, save it as a .gif file
                          Format: <gif-name>-ascii-art.gif
                          Gif will be saved in passed path
                          (pass . for current directory)
                          
      --save-bg ints      Set background color for --save-img
                          and --save-gif flags
                          Pass an RGBA value
                          e.g. --save-bg 255,255,255,100
                          (Defaults to 0,0,0,100)
                          
      --font string       Set font for --save-img and --save-gif flags
                          Pass file path to font .ttf file
                          e.g. --font ./RobotoMono-Regular.ttf
                          (Defaults to Hack-Regular for ascii and
                           DejaVuSans-Oblique for braille)
                          
      --font-color ints   Set font color for terminal as well as
                          --save-img and --save-gif flags
                          Pass an RGB value

import struct, zlib, sys

def make_png(path, w, h, fill=(128,128,128), stripes=False):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)  # filter
        for x in range(w):
            if stripes:
                # stripes pattern
                v = int(255 * (x + y) / (w + h))
                raw.extend([v, v, v])
            else:
                raw.extend(fill)
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)  # RGB
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

    raw = bytearray()

    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)

        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

make_grad("/tmp/grad_40x20.png", 40, 20)

print("ok")
EOF

import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            r,g,b = pixels[y*w + x]
            raw.extend([r,g,b])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# One pixel per value (0..255)

# Gradient at known positions
cat > /tmp/mkgrad2.py << 'EOF'
import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            r,g,b = pixels[y*w + x]
            raw.extend([r,g,b])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# One pixel per value (0..255)
W=256; H=1
px = [(i,i,i) for i in range(256)]
make_png("/tmp/grayline.png", W, H, px)

# 10 colors
px2=[(i*25, i*25, i*25) for i in range(10)]
make_png("/tmp/gray10.png", 10, 1, px2)
EOF
python3 /tmp/mkgrad2.py

echo "256-level grayscale linear:"
head -1 /tmp/out.txt
echo "==="
wc -l /tmp/out.txt
awk '{print length}' /tmp/out.txt

run_in_tty 100 10 "-d 10,1 /tmp/gray10.png"
echo "10-level:"
head -1 /tmp/out.txt

import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            r,g,b = pixels[y*w + x]
            raw.extend([r,g,b])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# L-shape:

# X..

cat > /tmp/mkasym.py << 'EOF'
import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h, pixels):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            r,g,b = pixels[y*w + x]
            raw.extend([r,g,b])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# L-shape: 
# X..
# X..
# XXX
px = [(255,255,255), (0,0,0), (0,0,0),
      (255,255,255), (0,0,0), (0,0,0),
      (255,255,255), (255,255,255), (255,255,255)]
make_png("/tmp/Lshape.png", 3, 3, px)
EOF

run_in_tty() {
    tmux new-session -d -s t -x "$1" -y "$2" "bash -c 'cd /workspace && ./executable ${*:3} > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; sleep 1'"
    sleep 2
    tmux kill-session -t t 2>/dev/null
}

# For ImgAspectRatio = iw/ih, default width = h * aspect * 2. Let me test with 40x20 (aspect 2), 40x30 (1.333)
cat > /tmp/mkrect.py << 'EOF'
import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            v = int((x+y)/(w+h)*255)
            raw.extend([v, v, v])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

make_png("/tmp/r40x30.png", 40, 30)
make_png("/tmp/r40x21.png", 40, 21)
make_png("/tmp/r31x13.png", 31, 13)
EOF
python3 /tmp/mkrect.py

for f in r40x30 r40x21 r31x13; do
    for size in "200 50" "100 50" "50 50"; do
        w=$(echo $size|cut -d' ' -f1)
        h=$(echo $size|cut -d' ' -f2)
        run_in_tty $w $h "/tmp/$f.png"
        cols=$(awk '{print length($0)}' /tmp/out.txt | sort -u | head -1)
        rows=$(wc -l < /tmp/out.txt)
        echo "  $f on ${w}x${h}: ${cols}x${rows}"
    done
done

import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            v = int(255 * x / (w-1))
            raw.extend([v, v, v])
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

make_png("/tmp/hgrad100x1.png", 100, 1)

import struct, zlib
def make_png(path, w, h, pixel):
    raw = bytearray()
    for y in range(h):
        raw.append(0)
        for x in range(w):
            raw.extend(pixel)
    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = zlib.crc32(tag + data)
        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data + struct.pack(">I", c)
    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    idat = zlib.compress(bytes(raw))
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", idat))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

# Test various scaling formulas
# For 20 -> 19 downsample, scale = 20/19 = 1.0526
# Lanczos kernel with radius 3 normally
# With support = 3*1.0526 = 3.158, and x /= scale

import math

def sinc(x):
    if x == 0: return 1
    return math.sin(math.pi * x) / (math.pi * x)

def lanczos3(x, radius=3):
    if abs(x) >= radius: return 0
    return sinc(x) * sinc(x/radius)

# For output row y in [0..18], compute center and weights
def compute_weights(src, dst, y, scale_support=True):
    scale = src / dst
    r = 3.0
    support = r * scale if scale > 1 and scale_support else r
    center = (y + 0.5) * scale - 0.5
    start = math.ceil(center - support)
    end = math.floor(center + support)
    if start < 0: start = 0
    if end > src - 1: end = src - 1
    weights = []
    for i in range(start, end + 1):
        x = i - center
        if scale > 1 and scale_support:
            x /= scale
        w = lanczos3(x)
        weights.append((i, w))
    s = sum(w for _,w in weights)
    weights = [(i, w/s) for i,w in weights]
    return center, weights

for y in [1, 8, 17, 18]:
    c, w = compute_weights(20, 19, y, scale_support=True)
    print(f"y={y} center={c:.3f}")
    for i, wt in w[:6]:
        print(f"  src[{i}] weight={wt:.4f}")
EOF

input.command:
run_in_tty() {
    local s="ss_$$_${RANDOM}${RANDOM}"
    tmux new-session -d -s "$s" -x "$1" -y "$2" "bash -c 'cd /workspace && $3 > /tmp/temp_out.txt 2>&1; sleep 0.5'"
    sleep 0.8
    tmux kill-session -t "$s" 2>/dev/null
}

mkdir -p /tmp/tests
for spec in "80 24" "200 50"; do
    w=$(echo $spec|cut -d' ' -f1)
    h=$(echo $spec|cut -d' ' -f2)
    for flags in "" "-c" "-n" "-f" "-b" "--dither -b" "-c -n" "-b -n" "-x" "-y" "-xy" "-d 30,15" "-W 40" "-H 20" "-b -d 20,10" "-m 'xyz'"; do
        for img in stripes_40x20 checker5 Lshape grad_40x20 gray_10x10; do
            cmd_mine="./executable_mine $flags /tmp/$img.png"
            cmd_orig="./executable $flags /tmp/$img.png"
            run_in_tty $w $h "$cmd_mine"
            cp /tmp/temp_out.txt /tmp/m.txt
            run_in_tty $w $h "$cmd_orig"
            cp /tmp/temp_out.txt /tmp/o.txt
            if ! diff -q /tmp/m.txt /tmp/o.txt >/dev/null; then
                d=$(diff /tmp/m.txt /tmp/o.txt | wc -l)
                echo "DIFF '$flags' $img ${w}x${h}: $d"
            fi
        done
    done
done
echo "done"

    local w=$1 h=$2
    shift 2
    
    tmux new-session -d -s s1 -x $w -y $h "cd /workspace && ./executable_mine $* > /tmp/mm.txt 2>&1; sleep 1"

# In setFlag, replace errors with CobraError

import re

# Match and replace
def sub_err(m):
    msg = m.group(1)
    # Strip "Error: " prefix
    if msg.startswith('Error: '):
        msg = msg[7:]
    return f'return &CobraError{{Message: fmt.Sprintf({msg!r})}}'

# Use a simpler approach: replace literal patterns
# The patterns have the form: return fmt.Errorf("Error: invalid argument %q for \"...\" flag", val)
# Convert to: return &CobraError{Message: fmt.Sprintf("invalid argument %q for \"...\" flag", val)}

src = re.sub(
    r'return fmt\.Errorf\("Error: (invalid argument %q for \\"[^"]+\\" flag)"([^)]*)\)',
    r'return &CobraError{Message: fmt.Sprintf("\1"\2)}',
    src,
)

open(path, 'w').write(src)

# Run all tests again to verify
for args in \
    "" \
    "/nonexistent" \
    "-d 10 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "-d 0,10 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "-d -1,10 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "-W -1 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "-H -1 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "-m x /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--threshold -1 -b /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--threshold 256 -b /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--threshold abc -b /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--font-color 0,0 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--font-color 256,0,0 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--save-bg 0,0,0 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--save-bg 0,0,0,101 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--save-bg 256,0,0,50 /tmp/Lshape.png" \
    "--invalid" \
    "--help" \
    "--version" \
    "--formats" \
    "-vC /tmp/Lshape.png"; do
    ./executable_mine $args > /tmp/mo.txt 2>/tmp/me.txt
    mex=$?
    ./executable $args > /tmp/oo.txt 2>/tmp/oe.txt
    oex=$?
    ok=1
    if [ "$mex" != "$oex" ]; then
        ok=0
    fi
    if ! diff -q /tmp/mo.txt /tmp/oo.txt > /dev/null || ! diff -q /tmp/me.txt /tmp/oe.txt > /dev/null; then
        ok=0
    fi
    if [ $ok -eq 1 ]; then
        echo "OK: $args"
    else
        echo "DIFF: $args (exit $mex vs $oex)"
        diff /tmp/mo.txt /tmp/oo.txt | head -3 | sed 's/^/  out: /'
        diff /tmp/me.txt /tmp/oe.txt | head -3 | sed 's/^/  err: /'
    fi
done
